security_audit.summary: The 92 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code spans, illustrative Worker code, safe secret-handling guidance, and public documentation URLs. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or hidden execution behavior was found. The skill does instruct users to retrieve and extract an unpinned package, which warrants controlled execution.

remediation.issue: Unpinned package download and archive extraction use a predictable shared temporary directory.
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before retrieval, pin or verify the package version and integrity, and use a unique restricted temporary directory that is removed after inspection.

remediation.issue: The retrieval workflow may make external network requests in environments with restrictive policies.
remediation.suggestion: State that documentation and package retrieval require network access and offer local installed types as the default fallback.

content.user_title: Review Cloudflare Workers with proven practices
content.value_statement: Cloudflare Workers projects can fail through outdated APIs, incorrect bindings, and unsafe runtime patterns. This skill guides code reviews and implementation using current documentation and focused production checks.
actual_capabilities: Reviews Worker handlers for streaming, promise handling, and request-scoped state.
Checks Wrangler configuration for compatibility dates, bindings, secrets, and observability.
Explains correct Env access patterns for module handlers and platform base classes.
Identifies insecure token generation and unsafe secret comparisons.
Suggests Workers-native bindings, Queues, Workflows, and Hyperdrive patterns.
Provides a structured review process with evidence and severity labels.
limitations: It does not execute, deploy, or test a Worker unless the host environment permits tools.
Current API guidance depends on successfully retrieving Cloudflare documentation and type definitions.
It cannot confirm production configuration, permissions, or runtime traffic without supplied access.
Examples require adaptation to the project's bindings, compatibility date, and requirements.

use_cases.title: Review a Worker before release
use_cases.description: Identify configuration, type, security, and runtime issues before a production deployment.

use_cases.title: Set up a new Worker project
use_cases.description: Create a configuration and handler structure that follows current Workers patterns.

use_cases.title: Standardize team reviews
use_cases.description: Apply a repeatable checklist for bindings, streaming, observability, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: review one handler
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Cloudflare Worker handler for the most important production issues. Explain each issue and show the corrected approach.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: check configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this wrangler.jsonc and Worker code together. Check binding names, secrets, compatibility settings, and observability.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: assess performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Worker for buffering, floating promises, global request state, and unnecessary network calls. Prioritize fixes by production impact.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: complete release review
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a release review of these Worker files. Retrieve current Workers guidance first, then report verified findings with severity, evidence, and remediation.

output_examples.input: Review a handler that stores the current user in a module variable.
output: High: request-scoped data is stored in module state and can leak between reused isolates.
Use function parameters or local variables for request-specific values.

output_examples.input: Review a configuration that stores an API key in vars.
output: High: the configuration contains a secret that can enter version control.
Store the value with Wrangler secrets and keep only non-secret settings in vars.

output_examples.input: Review a large upstream response that uses response.text().
output: Medium: buffering an unbounded response can exceed the Workers memory limit.
Return the response body as a stream or process it incrementally.

best_practices: Retrieve current Workers documentation and type definitions before making API-specific recommendations.
Provide file and line evidence for each finding and distinguish verified issues from suggestions.
Review configuration and source code together so binding names and secret handling stay consistent.
anti_patterns: Do not treat bundled examples as a substitute for the project's current Workers types and configuration.
Do not hardcode secrets or recommend storing credentials in Wrangler vars.
Do not buffer unbounded request or response bodies when streaming is appropriate.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews Cloudflare Workers code and Wrangler configuration for production practices, type safety, performance, and security.

faq.question: Does it use current Cloudflare guidance?
faq.answer: It instructs the assistant to retrieve current Cloudflare documentation and Workers type definitions before API-specific advice.

faq.question: Can it deploy my Worker?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and review findings. Deployment requires separate tools and authorization.

faq.question: Can it find secrets?
faq.answer: It checks for common hardcoded secret patterns and recommends Wrangler secret storage. It cannot guarantee that all credentials are detected.

faq.question: Does it support Durable Objects and Workflows?
faq.answer: It covers shared binding and class patterns, then directs specialized topics to the relevant documentation or skill.

faq.question: Should I run its package retrieval commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. Review the package name and network policy first. Use trusted registries and a controlled temporary directory.
